name: zsdx
why: A fan-made open Zelda engine port; a fun game but mostly a conventional, well-known style of game.

brief.what_it_is: Zelda: Mystery of Solarus DX is a free, fan-made action-RPG adventure and a direct sequel to The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past, using the same graphics and mechanics. The zsdx package contains only the game's data files, which the Solarus engine loads and runs, so you need Solarus installed to play. It is also an enhanced remake of Mystery of Solarus, a 2002 French-only game made with RPG Maker 2000. The homepage lists version 1.12.3 for Solarus 1.6.x.
brief.why_it_exists: The game was the first made with the Solarus engine, and the homepage says Solarus was primarily designed for it. The DX project was unveiled on April 1st, 2008 to fix the original's flaws, including the battle system, the bosses, and the use of items.
brief.how_it_works: The zsdx repository is a quest data package, not an engine. The solarus_run binary takes a quest path, either a directory with a data subdirectory or a directory containing a data.solarus zip archive. The CMake build packages the data into data.solarus and installs a zsdx launcher script that calls solarus_run with the installed quest path.

commands_seen.context: Runs the quest from the current directory, which must contain a data subdirectory (or data.solarus archive).
Runs the quest with no arguments; works only if Solarus was compiled with the default quest set to '.'.
Build step that generates the data.solarus archive containing all quest data files (the README gives these as two separate commands, cmake . then make).
Installs data.solarus to /usr/local/share/solarus/zsdx/ and a zsdx script to /usr/local/bin/ (assuming /usr/local prefix).
Launches the game after install; equivalent to solarus_run /usr/local/share/solarus/zsdx.
Configures the build to install to a custom prefix, for example without root access; followed by make and make install.

brief.install_notes: The README assumes Solarus is already installed; zsdx is a data package that needs the Solarus engine (the homepage targets Solarus 1.6.x). Building needs cmake and zip, which the README recommends. The default install goes to /usr/local and needs root; a custom prefix is possible via CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX. Beyond the brew formula, the README describes no accounts or runtime configuration beyond the build and install steps.
brief.standout: It is a full-length, professionally finished fan game built on an open-source engine, and the engine was designed around this game. The scout note calls it an 'engine port', but that is not accurate: it is a fan-made sequel and remake running on the Solarus engine, not a port of a Zelda game.
brief.status: quiet. The homepage lists v1.12.3 with a latest update on April 6, 2021, and the README describes a package that has not changed much. I did not see recent commit or release dates. The 'Latest update: August 17, 2026' line on the homepage is the page's own refresh stamp, not a project update, so I did not count it.
brief.caveats: The homepage lists three licenses: GPL v3, CC-BY-SA 4.0, and 'Proprietary (Fair use)'. The proprietary part is not explained, so check before redistributing. The game also needs a separate Solarus install and the Solarus 1.6.x line. The README gives no platform list, and I did not check how the brew formula packages the engine dependency.
quotes: The sequel to A Link to the Past, and the first game made with Solarus.
Mystery of Solarus DX was the first game made with the Solarus engine and in fact, Solarus was primarily designed for this game.
This quest is a free, open-source game that works with Solarus, an open-source Zelda-like 2D game engine.
